title: No fire. No lava. 1,700 dead.

scenes.text: One night in 1986, seventeen hundred people in Cameroon died in their sleep. No fire. No lava. No sound.
By morning, whole villages were silent. Most victims had not a single wound.
The killer was a lake. Lake Nyos suddenly released a giant cloud of carbon dioxide. Invisible. Odorless. Heavier than air.
It poured down the valleys and smothered everyone in its path.
And it can happen again, at a lake much bigger than this one. Full story on Oddly Logical Science. Subscribe for more true stories this strange.
